title: Opportunity Convergence Map — slope-adjusted prioritizer for token & latency regimes
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current RICE-based prioritization surfaces high-revenue, high-impact items but routinely overindexes features that look good on static metrics and fail under distinct runtime regimes (e.g., high-concurrency vs. latency-sensitive routes). This leads to rollout friction for Dedicated/Private customers and misalignment with constrained GPU capacity patterns.

Goal: Create a novel, production-facing prioritization artifact — the Opportunity Convergence Map (OCM) — and an accompanying slope-adjusted scoring function that augments RICE with (1) regime-specific cost multipliers (token and GPU marginal cost), (2) latency SLO risk slope, and (3) rollout friction penalty for infra changes. The result should be actionable prioritization buckets and an experimentable scoring formula that product, eng, and GTM can use for the next two roadmap cycles.

What success looks like: prioritization decisions that when simulated against past roadmap outcomes produce fewer SLA regressions and reduce projected incremental per-token cost for high-volume customers by >=8% on average across prioritized items.

Scope: PM-level scoring model + scoring workbook + integration guidance for Console roadmaps. Not in scope: automating scoring into Planner or changing billing models (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Deliver a one-page Opportunity Convergence Map visualization template with fields for Impact, Confidence, Effort, TokenMarginalCost, LatencyRiskSlope, RolloutFriction
Publish a slope-adjusted scoring function (text + worked examples) and a calculator workbook (CSV + Google Sheets) for reviewers
Run historical backtest on last 18 months of prioritized items and show metric delta vs. baseline RICE (SLA regressions, projected token delta)
Obtain alignment from Eng leads (runtime, infra), Design (Console), and Growth on scoring buckets and publish a rollout FAQ
Create 2 pilot decisions in Cycle 2025-W07 using the new score and document outcomes (A/B style decision log)
comments: 2025-01-16 — Priya Kapoor: Kickoff with Eng and Design. Agreed to prototype model in Sheets and to backtest against 18 months of roadmap decisions. Action: Marco to draft scoring formula.

2025-01-22 — Marco Jensen: First draft of slope-adjusted score uploaded to Drive (link below). Shared initial trade-offs: slope heavily penalizes features that add tail latency in <50ms routes. Need runtime sample distributions from Eng.

2025-01-25 — Diego Alvarez (Eng): Provided median & 95th pctl latency distributions for top 12 routes and token marginal cost per model. Noted that cost multipliers vary across Dedicated vs Hosted. Asked: do we expose per-customer multipliers or canonical regime templates?
2025-01-28 — Priya Kapoor: Decision to produce 3 canonical regimes (Lat-Sensitive, Throughput-Heavy, Mixed) to keep scoring tractable. Added 'regime' column to workbook.
2025-02-03 — Anika Rao (Design): Mocked OCM viz using heatmap + slope curves. Suggested explicit color lanes for risk buckets and a CTA to 'Escalate to Infra' for high-friction items.

2025-02-10 — Scott Meyer (PM Lead): Review feedback — refine rollout friction metric to include cross-team coordination effort and infra migration score. Also requested alignment with OKR impact scoring (weighed 60% by Outcome key results).
2025-02-12 — Marco Jensen: Incorporated Scott feedback; preparing final deck and shared PRD link. Requesting Eng + Design sign-off this week so we can pilot two decisions in Cycle 2025-W07.
decision_notes: Adopt a slope-adjusted function, defined as: Score = (Impact * Confidence) / (Effort * (1 + TokenMultiplier + LatencyRiskSlope + FrictionPenalty)). TokenMultiplier derived from marginal token/GPU cost delta for the primary regime; LatencyRiskSlope is a continuous penalty proportional to estimated p95 delta normalized to baseline; FrictionPenalty is a bounded [0,1] value reflecting infra migration complexity and cross-team coordination. We rejected per-customer multipliers for initial pilot to limit variability and instead use three canonical regimes. If pilot succeeds, follow-up will explore customer-weighted scoring.
tradeoffs: Pros: captures operational risk and cost, reduces SLA regression exposure, aligns product decisions with infra realities. Cons: introduces more inputs (data quality risk), requires runtime engineers to produce distributions, could add friction to fast 'flat' PM decisions. To mitigate, we provide templates, defaults, and a 1-click 'fast-override' with justification column for emergency decisions.
next_steps:
1) Finalize workbook & docs and obtain sign-offs by 2025-02-15. 2) Run 2 pilot prioritizations in Cycle 2025-W07. 3) Collect outcome metrics and iterate on penalty coefficients (2-week retro). 4) If pilot passes thresholds, schedule integration spec for Console decision UI in Q2.

Owners: PM: Priya Kapoor (strategy, OKR mapping), Eng: Marco Jensen (backtest & runtime signals), Design: Anika Rao (OCM visualization).
notes_for_reviewers: Key asks for reviewers: validate the LatencyRiskSlope definition against your runtime metrics, confirm canonical regime definitions, and sanity-check friction penalty banding. Please comment on Drive doc before 2025-02-15.
